questions.q: A biology student in Ibadan compares a palisade cell from a cassava leaf with a cheek cell from a rat. Which structure is present in the palisade cell but absent in the cheek cell?
questions.explanation: Palisade cells contain chloroplasts, which enable the plant cell to carry out photosynthesis. The cheek cell is an animal cell and does not contain chloroplasts, although both cells have a cell membrane, mitochondria and a nucleus.

questions.q: A freshwater Paramecium in a pond in Abeokuta has a contractile vacuole that fills and empties regularly. What is the main reason for this activity?
options: To digest food particles taken into the cell
To remove excess water that enters the cell by osmosis
To transport oxygen around the cell
questions.explanation: A freshwater Paramecium lives in a hypotonic medium, so water enters the cell by osmosis. The contractile vacuole collects and expels the excess water, preventing the cell from swelling and bursting. Digestion of food takes place in food vacuoles, not mainly in the contractile vacuole.

questions.q: A muscle cell from the leg of a footballer in Kaduna contains many mitochondria with highly folded inner membranes. This feature mainly increases the cell's capacity to
options: produce ATP for muscle contraction during respiration
absorb glucose directly from the blood
remove nitrogenous waste from the cytoplasm
store oxygen in the form of haemoglobin
questions.explanation: The folded inner membranes of mitochondria increase the surface area for the enzymes of aerobic respiration. This allows the cell to produce more ATP, which is needed for muscle contraction. Haemoglobin is found in red blood cells, not in mitochondria.

questions.q: A young potted tomato plant in Ilesa wilts at midday but becomes firm again in the cool evening. The recovery is mainly due to
options: water entering the parenchyma cells and increasing their turgor pressure
contraction of the stem muscles pulling the plant upright
increased formation of sclerenchyma fibres in the stem
lignin being deposited in the xylem vessels
questions.explanation: Young herbaceous plants are supported mainly by the turgidity of parenchyma cells. In the cooler evening, transpiration is reduced, so water enters the cells and restores turgor pressure. Lignin and sclerenchyma provide support in older plant parts, but they do not cause rapid recovery from wilting.

questions.q: A patient in Benin with healthy kidneys has glucose in the blood but normally none in the urine. This is because glucose is reabsorbed in the
questions.explanation: Glucose is filtered from the blood at the glomerulus and then selectively reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule. The Bowman's capsule collects the filtrate but does not carry out reabsorption of glucose. The collecting duct mainly reabsorbs water, and the ureter only carries urine away from the kidney.

questions.q: A mature cassava stem in Ogbomoso has small raised pores on its surface. These pores allow gaseous waste to leave the stem and are called
questions.explanation: Lenticels are small pores in the bark of woody stems that allow gaseous exchange and the escape of carbon dioxide. Stomata occur mainly on leaves and young green stems, while root hairs absorb water and mineral salts. Hydathodes mainly release water droplets from leaf margins.

questions.q: A blood sample from a student in Ilorin is left to stand and the cells settle. The pale yellow liquid above the cells forms the largest part of the blood volume and is called
questions.explanation: Plasma is the liquid part of blood and makes up the largest fraction of blood volume. Red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets are cellular components that settle below the plasma when blood is left to stand. Plasma transports dissolved substances such as glucose and urea.

questions.q: A leafy shoot of a hibiscus plant in Zaria takes up 45 cm³ of water in 15 minutes in a potometer. What is the rate of water uptake in cm³ per minute?
questions.explanation: The rate is obtained by dividing the volume of water taken up by the time taken: 45 cm³ ÷ 15 min = 3 cm³/min. The value 0.33 cm³/min would result from dividing the time by the volume instead of dividing the volume by the time.

questions.q: A bottle of perfume is opened at one corner of a classroom in Lagos. Before long, students at the far corner can smell it. Which statement best explains the observation?
options: Water molecules move across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to one of lower water potential.
The perfume is moved against a concentration gradient using energy from ATP.
The perfume reacts with oxygen in the air to form a gas that is carried around the room.
Perfume molecules move randomly from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
questions.explanation: The scent spreads by diffusion: perfume molecules move randomly down a concentration gradient from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated. Osmosis concerns water movement through a semi-permeable membrane, while active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and requires ATP.

questions.q: While gardening in Ibadan, a student sprinkles a little salt on a slug. The slug soon shrivels and dies mainly because
options: the salt is absorbed by active transport and blocks respiration in the slug's cells.
water moves out of the slug's body by osmosis into the stronger salt solution.
oxygen from the slug's body diffuses out faster than it enters.
the salt enters the slug by diffusion and makes its cells swell.
questions.explanation: The salt solution has a lower water potential than the slug's body fluids, so water leaves the body by osmosis and the animal shrivels. Salt does not enter by diffusion to cause swelling; the main effect is water loss.

questions.q: A biology student in Jos studies a cell that is moving a mineral ion across its membrane from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration. Which cell structure is most directly responsible for supplying the energy for this movement?
questions.explanation: Movement from a low to a high concentration is active transport, which requires ATP supplied mainly by mitochondria during aerobic respiration. The cell membrane is the site of the process, but it does not supply the energy.

questions.q: A woman in Minna has just ovulated. What happens to the ruptured follicle immediately after ovulation?
options: It becomes the placenta and secretes oestrogen.
It develops into the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.
It immediately produces another mature egg.
It is shed with the endometrium during menstruation.
questions.explanation: After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone to prepare and maintain the endometrium. The placenta forms after implantation, while menstruation occurs later if fertilisation does not take place.

questions.q: A gardener in Ibadan wants a flower to be cross-pollinated rather than self-pollinated. Which feature of the flower would best promote cross-pollination?
options: The stigma and anthers mature at different times.
The flower produces heavy pollen grains that fall directly onto its stigma.
The stigma is very close to the anthers.
The anthers and stigma mature at the same time.
questions.explanation: When the stigma and anthers mature at different times, self-pollination is less likely and pollen is more likely to come from another flower. Having the stigma close to the anthers, or anthers and stigma maturing together, makes self-pollination more likely.

questions.q: In a population of lizards on dark volcanic rocks in Jos, dark lizards are less easily seen by birds than light lizards. After many generations, the proportion of dark lizards increases. Which explanation best accounts for this?
options: The increase is caused only by random fertilisation among the lizards.
The lizards become dark because they need to blend with the rocks.
Dark lizards are produced because they eat dark-coloured insects.
Natural selection favours dark lizards because they survive and reproduce more successfully.
questions.explanation: Birds remove more light lizards, so dark lizards have a better chance of surviving and passing on their colour genes; this is natural selection. The idea that need causes a heritable change, or that diet alone changes inherited colour, is not supported by evolution by natural selection.

questions.q: A veterinary officer in Nsukka finds that some cattle have fluctuating fever, weight loss and swollen lymph nodes caused by trypanosomes. Which measure will most directly reduce the spread of the disease in the herd?
options: Removing ticks from the cattle with acaricide
Adding common salt to the cattle drinking water
Vaccinating all the cattle against anthrax
Controlling tsetse flies and treating infected cattle with appropriate drugs
questions.explanation: Trypanosomiasis is transmitted mainly by tsetse flies. Controlling the flies and treating infected cattle reduces both transmission and the source of parasites. Vaccination against anthrax, tick removal and salt in drinking water do not control tsetse-transmitted trypanosomes.

questions.q: A schoolchild in Lokoja is treated for ascariasis. Which practice will most directly prevent reinfection?
options: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated mosquito net
Washing hands with soap after defecation and before eating, and using a sanitary latrine
Wearing shoes when walking on moist soil
Boiling all drinking water for at least ten minutes
questions.explanation: Ascaris eggs are passed in faeces and become infective in contaminated soil, food or water. Using a sanitary latrine and washing hands after defecation and before eating prevent ingestion of the eggs. Footwear protects against hookworm, while a mosquito net and boiling water do not specifically stop reinfection by Ascaris.

questions.q: A bean seedling in a sealed transparent jar is kept in darkness for several hours. A dish of limewater inside the jar turns milky. Which process is directly responsible for this observation?
options: Photosynthesis by the seedling, releasing oxygen
Absorption of oxygen by the limewater
Respiration by the seedling, releasing carbon dioxide
Transpiration by the leaves, releasing water vapour
questions.explanation: The seedling is in darkness, so photosynthesis cannot occur. Aerobic respiration releases carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky. The other listed processes do not release carbon dioxide into the jar.

questions.q: After a student in Abuja runs a 400 m race, her breathing remains deep and rapid for several minutes. Which change in the blood most directly stimulates the breathing centre to maintain this increased breathing rate?
options: An increased concentration of carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: After exercise, carbon dioxide remains higher in the blood and is the main chemical stimulus to the breathing centre. This causes deeper and faster breathing until the excess is removed. A higher oxygen level does not stimulate breathing, and low glucose or low body temperature is not the direct stimulus here.

questions.q: A gardener in Abeokuta notices that young maize plants have poor root growth and leaves with a purplish tinge. Which mineral element is most likely deficient?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is needed for ATP, nucleic acids and healthy root development. Deficiency can cause stunted roots and a purplish tinge in maize leaves and stems. Nitrogen deficiency mainly causes general yellowing, magnesium deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis, and calcium deficiency affects growing tips.

questions.q: A stream near a farm in Ilorin receives runoff rich in fertilizers. Algae grow rapidly, then die and decompose. What is the most likely immediate effect on the stream?
options: Nitrate concentration falls to zero and plants grow faster
Dissolved oxygen decreases, so fish may die
The stream becomes more acidic and mosquito larvae are killed
Water temperature falls rapidly and algae disappear
questions.explanation: Fertilizer runoff causes rapid algal growth. When the algae die, decomposers use up dissolved oxygen, so fish and other animals may suffocate. This process is eutrophication.

questions.q: A bird in Kano is often seen feeding on ticks attached to the skin of cattle; the cattle are relieved of the ticks. Which type of ecological association is this?
questions.explanation: The bird obtains food from the ticks, while the cattle are freed from the parasites. Both partners benefit, so the association is mutualism. Parasitism benefits one and harms the other, commensalism benefits one without affecting the other, and competition harms both.

questions.q: In writing the scientific name of the maize plant as Zea mays, which rule of binomial nomenclature is being followed?
options: The whole scientific name is placed in quotation marks.
Both the genus name and the specific epithet begin with capital letters.
The specific epithet is written before the genus name.
The genus name begins with a capital letter while the specific epithet begins with a small letter.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word is the genus and is capitalised, while the second word is the specific epithet and starts with a lower-case letter. The name is conventionally italicised in print or underlined separately when handwritten, not quoted.

questions.q: In humans, the allele for dimples (D) is dominant to the allele for no dimples (d). A woman with no dimples marries a man who is heterozygous for dimples. What is the probability that their child will have dimples?
questions.explanation: The woman with no dimples has genotype dd, while the heterozygous man has genotype Dd. The possible offspring genotypes are Dd and dd in equal proportions, so half are expected to have dimples. A probability of 3/4 would require both parents to be heterozygous.

questions.q: A pea plant has genotype YyRr, with the two gene pairs on different chromosomes. Which set represents all the possible types of gametes the plant can form?
questions.explanation: Because the gene pairs are on different chromosomes, they assort independently during meiosis. Each gamete receives one allele from the Y/y pair and one from the R/r pair, giving YR, Yr, yR and yr. Gametes such as Yy or Rr contain two alleles of the same gene and are not normal haploid gametes.

questions.q: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion is folded into cristae. What is the main advantage of these folds?
options: They form the spindle fibres during cell division
They increase the surface area for respiratory reactions
They store water and mineral salts
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration involves enzymes and electron carriers located on the inner mitochondrial membrane. The cristae increase the membrane surface area, allowing more respiratory activity and energy release. Protein packaging is a function of the Golgi apparatus.

questions.q: A tomato plant growing in Ibadan has a young herbaceous stem that bends in the wind without breaking easily. Which tissue mainly provides this flexible support?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells have thickened corners but remain living and flexible, providing mechanical support to young growing stems. Sclerenchyma gives rigid support and is common in mature plant parts. Xylem conducts water and also strengthens older stems, while phloem transports sugars.

questions.q: When a student in Enugu lifts a bucket by bending the forearm at the elbow, the elbow joint acts as which part of a lever system?
questions.explanation: In the arm, the elbow joint is the pivot about which the forearm moves, so it acts as the fulcrum. The biceps supplies the effort, while the bucket provides the load. The forearm itself acts as the lever.

questions.q: Which part of the mammalian nephron is relatively impermeable to water while actively transporting sodium ions out of the tubule?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
questions.explanation: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but actively moves sodium ions into the medulla. This helps establish the high solute concentration needed for concentrating urine. The descending limb is permeable to water, while water movement in the collecting duct depends mainly on antidiuretic hormone.

questions.q: Which part of the mammalian kidney collects urine before it passes into the ureter?
questions.explanation: Urine formed by the nephrons drains into the renal pelvis, a funnel-like cavity that leads into the ureter. The cortex and medulla contain nephron structures and collecting ducts, while Bowman's capsule receives filtrate at the start of the nephron.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan compares blood in the pulmonary artery with blood in the pulmonary vein of a mammal. Compared with blood in the pulmonary vein, blood in the pulmonary artery has
options: the same oxygen concentration but a much higher glucose concentration
a higher oxygen concentration and a lower carbon dioxide concentration
a lower oxygen concentration and a higher carbon dioxide concentration
a higher concentration of oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, while the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Blood in the pulmonary artery therefore has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide than blood in the pulmonary vein.

questions.q: Blood flows most slowly through the capillaries mainly because
options: the total cross-sectional area of the capillary network is very large
the walls of the capillaries are only one cell thick
capillaries contain valves that resist blood flow
blood pressure is highest in the capillaries
questions.explanation: Although each capillary is very narrow, there are so many capillaries in parallel that their combined cross-sectional area is large. This slows blood flow and allows more time for exchange of materials. Thin walls help exchange, but they are not the main cause of the slow flow.

questions.q: A 50 g piece of pawpaw tissue is placed in distilled water. After 20 minutes, its mass has increased to 54 g. What is the percentage increase in mass?
questions.explanation: The increase in mass is 54 g − 50 g = 4 g. The percentage increase is (4 ÷ 50) × 100% = 8%. Water enters the tissue cells by osmosis, causing the observed increase in mass.

questions.q: A marine fish in a lagoon has body fluids with a lower salt concentration than the surrounding water. It secretes excess salts through special cells in its gills. Which process is mainly responsible for this salt secretion?
questions.explanation: The fish moves salts against a concentration gradient, from its body fluids into the surrounding water. This requires carrier proteins and energy from respiration, which are features of active transport. Osmosis concerns the movement of water, while simple diffusion would not move salts against the gradient.

questions.q: In a cross-section of a mammalian testis, which cells undergo the first meiotic division during the formation of sperm?
questions.explanation: Spermatogonia divide by mitosis to produce primary spermatocytes. The primary spermatocytes then undergo the first meiotic division to form secondary spermatocytes, which later divide again to form spermatids. Interstitial cells secrete testosterone and do not form sperm.

questions.q: A cocoa farmer in Ondo transfers pollen by hand from the anther of a high-yielding variety to the stigma of flowers of another healthy variety to obtain hybrid seeds. This practice is called
questions.explanation: The farmer deliberately transfers pollen from one plant variety to the stigma of another, so the process is artificial cross-pollination. It brings together gametes from two different varieties, increasing genetic variation. Double fertilisation occurs inside the ovule after pollination, not during the transfer of pollen.

questions.q: A gardener in Jos crosses a pure-breeding red-flowered plant with a pure-breeding white-flowered plant. All the F₁ plants produce red flowers. When the F₁ plants are self-pollinated, 400 seeds are obtained. How many of the resulting plants are expected to produce white flowers?
questions.explanation: Since all F₁ plants are red, red is dominant and the F₁ genotype is Rr. Self-pollination gives a 3 red : 1 white ratio, so the expected number of white-flowered plants is 1/4 × 400 = 100.

questions.q: Biochemical studies show that the DNA base sequences of humans and chimpanzees are very similar. This observation is best used as evidence that the two species
questions.explanation: Similar DNA base sequences indicate a close evolutionary relationship and a common ancestor. They do not mean the two species are in the same genus, have identical proteins, or can interbreed freely.

questions.q: Musa in Kano skipped lunch and his blood glucose level fell. Which hormone is secreted to raise the blood glucose level?
questions.explanation: Glucagon is secreted by the pancreas and stimulates the liver to break down glycogen into glucose. Insulin lowers blood glucose, antidiuretic hormone affects water reabsorption, and thyroxine mainly increases metabolic rate.

questions.q: A child in Ilesa is brought to a clinic with fever, cough, runny nose, and a red rash that started on the face. Which disease is most likely?
questions.explanation: Measles typically causes fever, cough, runny nose and a spreading red rash, and it is prevented by vaccination. Malaria and typhoid fever do not usually show this combination of symptoms, while chickenpox rash commonly starts on the trunk with vesicles.

questions.q: A nurse in Kaduna gives a newborn baby the BCG vaccine. This vaccine is given mainly to protect the child against
questions.explanation: BCG vaccine protects against tuberculosis, especially severe forms in young children. Poliomyelitis, measles and tetanus are prevented by their own specific vaccines.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the human heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood to the left atrium, while the aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle and the vena cava returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium.

questions.q: In a population of grasshoppers on a school field in Oyo, which factor is density-dependent?
options: The daily temperature of the field.
The amount of rainfall during the term.
A sudden bush fire passing through the field.
Competition for food among the grasshoppers.
questions.explanation: A density-dependent factor has an effect that becomes stronger as the population becomes larger, such as competition for food. Rainfall, bush fire and temperature act independently of population size and are density-independent. Thus competition for food is the only factor whose impact depends on how many grasshoppers are present.

questions.q: In a grassland food chain near Kano, the producers contain 1,000 kJ of energy. If only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
questions.explanation: Primary consumers receive 10% of 1,000 kJ, which is 100 kJ. Secondary consumers receive 10% of 100 kJ, which is 10 kJ. The value 100 kJ is the energy reaching primary consumers only.

questions.q: A plant growing in Sokoto has leaves with sunken stomata and a thick waxy cuticle. These features mainly help the plant to…
options: increase the rate of respiration in the leaf.
increase the absorption of mineral salts from the soil.
questions.explanation: Sunken stomata and a thick waxy cuticle reduce evaporation from the leaf surface, helping the plant conserve water in a dry habitat. Mineral salts are absorbed mainly by roots, and respiration is not increased by these leaf features. These structures also do not help attract pollinators.

questions.q: A factory worker in Eleme develops a mutation in a skin cell after exposure to radiation. Why is this mutation unlikely to be passed on to his children?
options: A recessive mutation can never be inherited by offspring.
Radiation cannot alter the genetic material of humans.
The affected skin cells cannot divide to form new cells.
The mutation occurred in a somatic cell, not in the gametes.
questions.explanation: Only mutations in gametes, such as sperm or egg cells, can be transmitted to offspring during fertilisation. A mutation in a skin cell is a somatic mutation and affects only that individual's body cells. Recessive mutations can still be inherited when present in gametes and combined with another recessive allele.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the sex chromosomes of a normal human female?
options: There are two X chromosomes, both inherited from the mother.
There are two X chromosomes, one inherited from each parent.
There is one X chromosome and one Y chromosome, both inherited from the mother.
There is one X chromosome from the mother and one Y chromosome from the father.
questions.explanation: A normal human female has two X chromosomes, one from the mother's egg and one from the father's sperm. A Y chromosome from the father would normally produce a male. Therefore the two X chromosomes must come one from each parent, not both from the mother.

questions.q: A scientist in Yaba places a living amoeba in a drop containing a dye. The dye enters the cytoplasm while large protein molecules do not. The structure mainly responsible for this selective uptake is the
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and controls the entry and exit of substances. The nuclear membrane surrounds the nucleus, while a food vacuole membrane encloses a vacuole rather than the whole cytoplasm.

questions.q: A biology student in Makurdi examines the vertebral column of a rabbit. Which vertebra has a long neural spine and articulates with ribs?
questions.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae bear ribs and have long neural spines for muscle attachment. Cervical vertebrae are in the neck, lumbar vertebrae do not bear ribs, and sacral vertebrae are fused to form part of the pelvis.

questions.q: A mature plant stem in Ogbomoso is strengthened mainly by dead cells with thick lignified walls. These cells form the
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma fibres are dead cells with thick lignified walls and give mechanical strength to mature plant parts. Collenchyma and parenchyma are living cells with thinner walls, while sieve tubes are involved in sugar transport.

questions.q: A man in Ibadan eats a protein-rich meal. During deamination in the liver, toxic ammonia is converted to
questions.explanation: The liver converts toxic ammonia from deamination into less toxic urea, which is carried in the blood to the kidneys for removal. Glucose is not a nitrogenous waste, and uric acid is the main nitrogenous waste in many birds and insects.
